meetTheTeam.title: Meet The Team
meetTheTeam.subtitle: How we got here and created The A Team Project
meetTheTeam.originHeading: The best people they'd ever worked with were people they'd worked with before.
meetTheTeam.paragraph1End: —former work besties—had an epiphany: the best people they'd ever worked with were... people they'd worked with before.
meetTheTeam.paragraph2: Looking at today's tech hiring mess (AI-generated resumes fooling AI filters, anyone?), they saw their chance. While recruiters drown in fake applications and accidentally filter out diverse talent, The A Team Project was born with a simple idea:
meetTheTeam.paragraph3: Skip the LinkedIn humble-brags and AI recruiting arms race. Instead, build an exclusive network where top tech talent refers top tech talent. Because the best people know the best people—and
meetTheTeam.paragraph3Bold: life's too short not to work with good people.
meetTheTeam.edBio: Detail-oriented UX designer. Previously built Waldo, a startup organization tool, alongside Hova.
meetTheTeam.hovaBio: Co-founder of Hova Labs, a creative engineering studio. Writes about design systems, AI, and building teams.

meetChippy.title: Meet Chippy
meetChippy.subtitle: The brave little parrot who became the face of our AI
meetChippy.photoAlt: A photo of Chippy, a bright red and blue parrot
meetChippy.paragraph1: While we were building The A Team Project at Hova's house, a little lost parrot turned up outside the kitchen window — bright, curious, and a long way from home.
meetChippy.paragraph2: Over the next two days we earned their trust the old-fashioned way: apples, patience, and Hova channeling her full inner Disney princess. Eventually the brave little adventurer hopped inside to safety.
meetChippy.paragraph3: That same warmth and resiliency is the spirit we wanted at the heart of our human-centric AI — so we named it after him. Meet Chippy, our matchmaker and our mascot.

accessibility.title: ACCESSIBILITY STATEMENT
accessibility.intro: The A Team Project is committed to making our website accessible to everyone, including people with disabilities. We want every visitor — however they browse the web — to be able to explore our work, meet the team, and use our tools with confidence. This statement describes how we approach accessibility, where we stand today, and how to reach us if something gets in your way.
accessibility.conformanceDescription: The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) define requirements for designers and developers to improve accessibility for people with disabilities. They define three levels of conformance: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA. The A Team Project aims to conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, and we build accessibility into how we design, develop, and review the site. Some parts of the site may not yet fully conform; where that is the case, we are actively working to fix it.
accessibility.measuresTitle: Measures we take to support accessibility
accessibility.measuresDescription: To make and keep The A Team Project accessible, we work to:
accessibility.measure1: Use semantic HTML and ARIA landmarks, with a "skip to main content" link, so assistive technologies can navigate each page.
accessibility.measure2: Provide text alternatives for meaningful images and icons, and hide purely decorative graphics from screen readers.
accessibility.measure3: Associate every form field with a label so its purpose is announced to assistive technology.
accessibility.measure4: Make all interactive controls fully operable with a keyboard.
accessibility.measure5: Manage focus in dialogs and menus — moving focus in, keeping it inside, and returning it to where you were when they close.
accessibility.measure6: Maintain readable color contrast in both light and dark themes, with visible focus indicators.
accessibility.measure7: Keep the layout responsive so content reflows and stays usable when zoomed or on small screens.
accessibility.measure8: Respect the operating system "reduce motion" setting for animations.
accessibility.measure9: Offer the site in more than one language.
accessibility.compatibilityTitle: Compatibility with browsers and assistive technology
accessibility.compatibilityDescription: The A Team Project is designed to work with recent versions of major browsers — Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge — on both desktop and mobile, and with common assistive technologies such as screen readers, screen magnifiers, and voice-recognition software. It may not work as well with older browsers that no longer receive security or standards updates.
accessibility.technicalDescription: Accessibility of The A Team Project relies on the following technologies to work with your browser and any assistive technologies you use: HTML, WAI-ARIA, CSS, and JavaScript. These technologies are relied upon for conformance with the accessibility standards used.
accessibility.thirdPartyDescription: Some parts of our site rely on third-party services that we do not fully control — for example, signing in with LinkedIn, a bot-protection challenge (Cloudflare Turnstile), and links to external websites. We choose accessible options where we can and offer alternatives when a third-party experience falls short. If a third-party feature blocks you, please contact us and we will help.
accessibility.assessmentDescription: We evaluate the accessibility of The A Team Project in the following ways:
accessibility.assessment1: Self-evaluation as we design and build features.
accessibility.assessment2: Manual keyboard-only testing of interactive flows.
accessibility.assessment3: Testing with screen readers and other assistive technology.
accessibility.assessment4: Reviewing pages against WCAG 2.2 Level AA success criteria.
accessibility.assessment5: Incorporating feedback from the people who use the site.
accessibility.limitationsDescription: Despite our efforts, some content may not yet be fully accessible. Known limitations include:
accessibility.limitation1: Embedded third-party widgets and challenges, whose accessibility we cannot fully control.
accessibility.limitation2: External links, which lead to sites whose accessibility we cannot guarantee.
accessibility.limitation3: Some older marketing graphics and downloadable files, which may not be fully tagged.
accessibility.limitationsClose: If you run into a barrier that isn't listed here, please tell us — your report helps us find and prioritize a fix.
accessibility.feedbackDescription: We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of The A Team Project. If you encounter a barrier or have a suggestion, you can use the in-app feedback button on any page, or email us at
accessibility.responseTime: We aim to respond within five business days.
accessibility.statementDate: This statement was created on August 12, 2026, and is reviewed as the site evolves.

jobScout.title: Job Scout
jobScout.subtitle: Run the daily job-matching cron by hand and see exactly what it did.
jobScout.runningNote: This can take a few minutes.

confirm.title: This ignores everyone's schedule
confirm.ignores: A manual run is a forced run. Up to 25 users get matched right now — least-recently-scouted first — including anyone already scouted in the last 20 hours and anyone paused for the weekend.
confirm.resumes: Nothing changes permanently. This run stamps everyone it matches as scouted, so the daily 15:00 UTC (7am PST) cron skips them until their usual gap has passed — 20 hours on daily, 156 hours on weekly. The normal cadence picks back up on its own from there.
confirm.duplicates: It can't create duplicate matches: a posting already matched to a user is never matched to them again.

jobScout.errorGeneric: The run failed. Check the server logs.
jobScout.errorUnauthorized: Your session expired or you lost admin access — sign in again.

digest.title: Digest emails
digest.description: The other half of the scout: emails each due user the matches they haven't been sent yet. Same tick as the 16:00 UTC cron, run now.

confirm.title: This sends real email
confirm.sends: Every user who is due right now gets their digest immediately — up to 200 of them, longest-waiting first. There is no undo once mail is out the door.
confirm.respects: It does not ignore anyone's schedule. Only users with digest emails on, who are past their gap (20 hours on daily, 156 hours on weekly) and not paused for the weekend, are due. Anyone emailed this morning is not.
confirm.stamps: Matches included in a digest are marked as sent, so the next run won't repeat them — and a user's next digest is measured from now.

runs.title: Run history
runs.description: Every job-scout tick from the last 30 days. Download a run's CSVs to see what it parsed off the boards, what it matched and why, and what it dropped and why — per user.
runs.empty: No runs recorded yet. Trigger one above, or wait for tonight's cron.

workHistory.howToExportSummary: How do I get this export from LinkedIn?
howToExportSteps: Open LinkedIn's "Get a copy of your data" page.
LinkedIn emails you a download link, usually within a day. If it hasn't arrived, check your spam folder — or just revisit the link from step 1 the next day to download the archive directly.
Unzip the file and upload the {{file}} here.

preferences.companyStageSeedTradeoff: Biggest equity upside and the most influence on direction — but the highest risk. Expect to wear many hats with little structure.
preferences.companyStageSeriesATradeoff: Finding product-market fit. Still high equity and scrappy, with teams and process just starting to form.
preferences.companyStageSeriesBTradeoff: Scaling a proven model. Faster growth and more defined roles, with moderate equity and more stability.
preferences.companyStageSeriesCPlusTradeoff: Established and stable, with clear career paths and higher base pay — but less equity upside and less individual impact.
